content:
Stephanie Nguyen: We need to settle the pricing slide for Standard Demo v1. AEs keep asking for “a number” but I’m worried we’re going to get pinned down live.

Soojin Lee: Yeah, slide 12 currently has $/1M tokens placeholders + a “50% cheaper” callout. I’m not comfortable shipping that without hard sourcing + versioning.

Markus Klein: +1. In a live demo, the moment you show a number, it becomes the contract in the prospect’s brain. Also varies a lot by model, context length, batching, etc.

Jordan Blake: Agree. We want to show *economics levers* and *ranges*, not list prices. If someone asks for pricing, we route to “we’ll scope based on your workload” + a follow-up.

Camila Reyes: Marketing POV: anything with specific dollars needs legal + finance blessing and can’t be tied to a single competitor unless we have citations we’re ready to defend. “Up to X%” claims need clear conditions.

Stephanie Nguyen: Field feedback: procurement teams are screenshotting decks. If we ship a deck with numbers, it will leak and/or create mismatch with what Finance quotes.

Ben Carter: From Growth/Sales Ops side: also messes with our demo-to-eval funnel. AEs use the deck as a “price anchor” and then we see drop when quote differs.

Nikhil Sharma: Product: we *can* safely talk about “token-level cost visibility” and “unit cost improvements via batching/caching/quantization.” But hard $ figures depend on tenant config and hardware pool.

Soojin Lee: Proposal: keep the slide, but make it “Cost controls (not list price)” and show ranges like:
- “Typical savings: 20–60% vs baseline unoptimized serving”
- “Latency/cost tradeoff knobs”
And footnote: “Ranges vary by model + workload; validated in Redwood internal benchmarks.”

Markus Klein: That’s closer. But even “20–60%” could be challenged. We need a source doc that PMM approves.

Camila Reyes: We have the “Benchmark Proof Points - Slides Inputs” table in Drive. But it’s still marked working. If we use ranges, we need to stick to the “safe-to-say” columns only.

Stephanie Nguyen: Can we just remove the slide entirely? Replace with “How we price” (usage + dedicated + private) and “what impacts cost” without ranges.

Jordan Blake: I prefer we keep *something* because economics is a key differentiator. But it should be framed as: “We help you manage and reduce inference cost” not “here’s our price.”

Isabelle Laurent: Also: CRM workflow. If prospect is in procurement mode, we should not try to “close pricing” in the demo. We should capture their expected volume + deployment mode and schedule a pricing call.

Markus Klein: In demos I usually say:
- Hosted: usage-based, pay for what you use
- Dedicated: reserved capacity, predictable throughput
- Private: platform fee + support tier
Then I pivot to Console cost dashboard and show relative changes when we tweak batching/routing.

Soojin Lee: Ok what if slide becomes:
1) Pricing model (no numbers)
2) What drives total cost (tokens, context length, concurrency, routing)
3) Proof: “Console shows per-route token cost + latency”
No competitor comparison, no $.

Camila Reyes: That is 100% safer. We can keep *one* “range” statement, but only if it’s phrased as “teams commonly see meaningful savings when…” without a %.

Stephanie Nguyen: I like no ranges. The minute you show a range, they ask “where will we land?” and we’re back in the weeds.

Jordan Blake: Let’s decide: no numbers and no % ranges in the standard deck. We can have an internal-only appendix for trained reps with “if asked” guidance.

Markus Klein: +1. And in the talk track we can say: “We’ll give you a workload-specific estimate in an eval—here’s how we measure it.”

Ben Carter: Works for instrumentation too. We can track “pricing asked?” as a checkbox in HubSpot notes instead of trying to answer on the spot.

Soojin Lee: Cool. I’ll update the deck:
- Remove $/token placeholders
- Replace with “Pricing & economics” slide (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) + “Cost drivers” slide
- Add speaker note: “Do not quote numbers. Offer ranges only in follow-up.”

Camila Reyes: Please send me the exact wording before you lock. We should align on: “Pricing depends on model, throughput, and deployment mode” + “we’ll scope with you.”

Stephanie Nguyen: Also add an objection-handling snippet:
If they insist: “We can share pricing after 2–3 questions” and propose next step.

Markus Klein: I’ll add a sidebar for SEs:
If asked for per-token: “We don’t publish a single number because optimization + routing affects it; we’ll estimate using your traffic shape.”

Jordan Blake: Decision: Standard Demo Deck v1 has no pricing numbers. Show pricing *structure* + economic levers + cost observability proof. If asked, commit to follow-up with scoped quote.

Soojin Lee: Got it. I’ll push a v1.0 update today and tag you all for review. :thumbsup:

Camila Reyes: :white_check_mark: Works. Send the updated slide text + speaker notes.

Stephanie Nguyen: Thanks. This will save us a lot of weird calls. :pray:
